html:
The Pit River people are the Indigenous peoples of the Pit River valley in northeastern California: the Achumawi and the Atsugewi. Today they form the Pit River Tribe, made up of eleven bands.

They lived by fishing, hunting deer and gathering roots, seeds and acorns. The river got its English name from the pits they dug to trap game. During the Gold Rush of the 1850s settlers and militias killed many of them and took their land. Their neighbours were the Modoc to the north and the Shasta to the west. The Pit River joins the Sacramento at Shasta Lake, where the Shasta Dam flooded part of their lands.
